drift_changes.description: Added RefundPayment function to process payment refunds when orders are cancelled
drift_changes.root_cause_rationale: During testing, discovered that order cancellation doesn't trigger payment refund. This wasn't considered in initial design but is required for business logic. Users were being charged for cancelled orders, which is operationally unacceptable.
drift_changes.impact: HIGH - Customers charged for cancelled orders without refund

architectural_impact.functional_flows: Update FLOW-003 (Order Cancellation) to include RefundPayment step

drift_changes.description: Added GetPaymentStatus function and payment_status_query interface to enable OrderService to query payment status
drift_changes.root_cause_rationale: Initial requirements didn't specify that order status should include payment information. During testing and stakeholder review, this was identified as necessary for customer service and user experience. Requirement was incomplete, not a design flaw.
drift_changes.impact: MEDIUM - Incomplete information to users/customer service

architectural_impact.functional_flows: Update FLOW-002 (Order Status Query) to include GetPaymentStatus step

drift_changes.description: Added ValidateOrderUniqueness function to prevent race conditions during concurrent order creation
drift_changes.root_cause_rationale: Order ID generation used timestamp-based approach which fails under concurrent load. Need atomic uniqueness validation before order creation. This is a technical constraint (race condition) that wasn't identified until concurrency testing.
drift_changes.impact: HIGH - System crashes under concurrent load

architectural_impact.functional_flows: Update FLOW-001 (Order Creation) to include ValidateOrderUniqueness as first step
